svg.text: The Big Picture — Networking: the school post · the post room is in the repo
📮 PART 1 — THE POST (lessons 1–6)
📮 an address, a room, a road (1–3)
IP address = the building · port = the room
a socket = one desk: (ip:port ↔ ip:port)
192.168.0.0/24 = the wing · NAT at the gate
📦 the delivery chain (4)
letter (HTTP) → envelope (TCP/UDP) →
bag (IP) → van (Ethernet/Wi-Fi) → road
each layer reads only its own label
📬 registered post vs the loudspeaker (5)
TCP: handshake, receipts, order — a stream
UDP: shout once, some are lost — datagrams
you add message boundaries to a stream
📖 the directory (6)
a name → an address, asked over UDP 53
root → .com → example.com · TTL = how long to remember
'is it DNS?' is question one of every outage
🐍 net/demo.py — the post room, zero dependencies
tcp · udp · ports · dns (a 29-byte question by hand) · http (typed onto a socket) · tls (reads the certificate) · route
every section is one lesson; run one, read the twenty lines behind it, then run the real tool beside it
⚠️ the two mistakes every first outage makes
debugging the app (L7) when the name (DNS) or the gate (firewall) is the fault —
and reading 'timed out' as 'server down' when it means 'the gate dropped you'
python3 net/demo.py · bash net/lab.sh example.com — the whole course, in two commands
🏗️ PART 2 — THE BUILDING (lessons 7–12)
📨🔒 the slip and the seal (7–8)
HTTP is text on a stream: request line, headers,
blank line, body · /1.1 keep-alive, /2 multiplexed, /3 QUIC
TLS: a certificate a CA signed, then a sealed envelope
expiry and wrong names break the seal
🧭🚧 corridors and the gate (9–10)
a route: prefix → next hop; nobody has the whole map
traceroute shows every porter · MTU ~1500
firewall: allow-lists, stateful · refused vs timed out
NAT rewrites the from-address · VPN = a tunnel inside
🏪 the reception desk (11)
load balancer: L4 by ip:port · L7 by URL
health checks skip a sick counter · TLS ends here
CDN: a copy of the notice board in every city
Kubernetes Service / Ingress · AWS NLB / ALB
🔧 the ladder (12)
DNS → ping → traceroute → nc → openssl → curl -v → logs
the first rung that fails names the cause
latency ≠ bandwidth · NXDOMAIN, refused, timed out, reset
capstone: a one-page runbook per service
🧭 read one envelope, read them all: address → room → road → contract → name → seal → gate → desk
every 'it's down' is one of seven questions, asked in order · siblings: the API school fills the envelope · AWS rents the building · Kubernetes puts a desk in every cluster
